complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Migrate Windows Hook Implementation to Rust
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break this down into: 1) Research and setup windows-rs dependencies and FFI bindings, 2) Implement mouse hook callback function with MSLLHOOKSTRUCT handling, 3) Implement keyboard hook callback with KBDLLHOOKSTRUCT and VK_LWIN suppression, 4) Create thread-safe hook management with proper install/uninstall, 5) Integrate Windows message pump with Tauri's async runtime, 6) Add comprehensive error handling and resource cleanup
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: This is the most complex task requiring deep Windows API knowledge, unsafe Rust code, FFI bindings, and careful threading considerations. The existing C++ code shows significant complexity with hook callbacks, message pumps, and resource management.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break into: 1) Install SignalDB dependencies and setup basic reactive store, 2) Design and implement configuration schema with validation, 3) Implement persistent storage to %APPDATA% with file I/O handling, 4) Integrate with SolidJS reactivity system and create type-safe interfaces
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Moderate complexity involving new library integration, filesystem operations, and reactive state management. SignalDB is not currently in package.json, requiring research and setup.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break into: 1) Research and setup Tauri v2 system tray plugin, 2) Implement tray icon creation with existing app.ico, 3) Create context menu with Show/Hide, hook toggles, and Exit options, 4) Implement window show/hide behavior and tray click handlers, 5) Add dynamic tray tooltips and icon updates based on hook status
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: High complexity due to Tauri v2 system tray API changes, window management, and cross-platform considerations. Requires deep integration with OS-specific features.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break into: 1) Replace default App.tsx with configuration layout and styling, 2) Create toggle switch components connected to SignalDB reactive state, 3) Add status indicators and implement real-time UI updates based on hook states
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Moderate complexity. SolidJS is already set up, but requires complete UI overhaul and reactive state integration. The existing App.tsx is basic template code.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break into: 1) Add winreg crate dependency and setup registry access functions, 2) Implement add_to_startup() function with proper registry key creation, 3) Implement remove_from_startup() with error handling for missing keys, 4) Create Tauri commands and frontend integration with UAC permission handling
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Significant complexity involving Windows registry manipulation, permission handling, and Tauri command integration. Registry operations are error-prone and require careful permission management.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Create Tauri Commands for Hook Management
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break into: 1) Design thread-safe state management architecture using tauri::State, 2) Implement enable_hooks() and disable_hooks() commands with proper error handling, 3) Create toggle_windows_key_hook() and toggle_mouse_button_hook() commands, 4) Implement get_hook_status() with comprehensive status reporting, 5) Integrate commands with existing hook implementation and frontend
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: High complexity due to thread-safety requirements, state management across Rust backend and frontend, and integration with low-level Windows hooks. Requires careful architecture to avoid race conditions.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break into: 1) Research MSLLHOOKSTRUCT.mouseData parsing for buttons 5-8, 2) Extend mouse hook callback to detect additional button presses, 3) Add configuration options for each extended button in schema and UI, 4) Implement hardware detection and fallback behavior for unsupported buttons
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Moderate-high complexity requiring deep Windows API knowledge for extended mouse button detection. Current C++ code only handles buttons 3-4, so this extends that functionality significantly.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break into: 1) Adapt existing app.ico for all required Tauri icon formats and update tauri.conf.json, 2) Update application metadata, window titles, and ensure consistent branding across system tray and main window
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Low complexity. Icons already exist in the project (app.ico in InhibitWindowsEvents folder and various PNG formats in src-tauri/icons). Mainly configuration and file operations.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break into: 1) Implement default configuration object with Mouse Button 4 enabled as specified, 2) Add first-run detection and configuration initialization logic, 3) Implement configuration migration system for future updates
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Moderate complexity involving initialization logic, first-run detection, and configuration migration patterns. Requires integration with SignalDB configuration system from Task 2.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break into: 1) Setup structured logging with log/tracing crate and configure output destinations, 2) Add comprehensive error handling for Windows API calls and hook operations, 3) Implement user-friendly error messages in UI and system tray notifications, 4) Add configurable debug logging for hook events and graceful degradation strategies
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Moderate complexity involving logging framework setup, error handling patterns, and user feedback systems. Needs integration across the entire application stack from Windows hooks to UI.
